newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco stocks strong as settlement appears near.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco stocks strong as settlement appears near.

text.p: Tobacco stocks rallied Monday amid speculation that a settlement to resolve mounting litigation against the industry could be reached within two to three weeks, analysts said.

Philip Morris, the most heavily-traded issue on the New York Stock Exchange, settled to 43, up 5/8, after hitting a high of 43-3/4 in early morning trading. RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp added 3/8 to 31-3/8.
"There's continued speculation that they could be within two weeks of reaching an agreement," said Martin Feldman, a tobacco analyst with Smith Barney.
Morgan Stanley reiterated strong buy rating on both Philip Morris and RJR Nabisco.
Market rumors suggested a possible settlement may limit the tobacco industry's liability to $4 billion a year, but investors reacted with caution, analysts said.

"The market is still uncertain. Philip Morris is up more than a dollar, but if people really believed the settlement were very close, they'd be up more than that. The market is still very cautious," Feldman said.
Reports of a potential settlement have been surfacing from the plaintiff's camps, while the tobacco companies have remained silent, analysts said.

"I haven't heard anything at all from the tobacco side ... this could be a lot of propaganda here. I just hear so many numbers that it raises a lot of questions," said John Maxwell, an analyst with Wheat First Butcher Singer.
Philip Morris and RJR Nabisco could not be reached for comment.
The American Stock Exchange Tobacco Index .TOB gained 3.10 points or 1.04 percent to 300.20.
